lines: +- Support partial function application (PHP 8.6), such as `f(1, ?)`, `f(1, ...)`, `$obj->method(?, 2)` or `f(b: ?, a: 1)`. This needs php-ast 1.1.5+, which provides the arguments in AST version 130; Phan uses that version when the installed php-ast supports it, and version 120 otherwise. With an older php-ast, partial function application cannot be told apart from first-class callable syntax (`f(...)`) and is still analyzed like it.

+  - The type of the expression is a closure with the parameters that are left, e.g. `Closure(int $b):int` for `add3(1, ?, 3)`: a parameter for each `?` (required, also when the parameter of the function is optional), the parameters of named placeholders in the order they are written, and the remaining parameters for `...`. Calls of the closure are checked against those parameters.

+  - The arguments that are bound to values are checked against the parameters of the function when the closure is created, and so is the number of arguments (`PhanTypeMismatchArgument`, `PhanParamTooMany`, `PhanParamTooFew`, ...).
+  - `$x |> f(1, ?)` and `$x |> f(1, ...)` pass `$x` in the place of the placeholder.
+  - Add `PhanCompatiblePartialApplication` (critical), emitted when `minimum_target_php_version` is older than 8.6.

- Report the functions, methods and constants deprecated in PHP 8.6 when `target_php_version` is 8.6 or newer, with any PHP version running Phan: `is_double()`, `is_integer()`, `is_long()`, `doubleval()`, `strcoll()`, `metaphone()`, `spl_classes()`, `spl_object_hash()`, the `mb_ereg*()` functions, `mb_split()`, `mb_regex_encoding()` and `mb_regex_set_options()` (`PhanDeprecatedFunctionInternal`), the sorting, flag and serialization methods of `ArrayIterator` and the CSV methods of `SplFileObject` (`PhanDeprecatedFunctionInternal`), and the constants `SORT_LOCALE_STRING` and `MB_ONIGURUMA_VERSION` (`PhanDeprecatedGlobalConstant`). Functions and methods declared by Phan's stubs, such as `spl_object_hash()` and the SPL methods, were not reported even when running PHP 8.6

- Add `PhanDeprecatedReservedName`, emitted when `target_php_version` is 8.6 or newer for the declaration of a function named `let`, `is` or `readonly`, a class, interface, trait or enum named `let` or `is`, or a class constant named `namespace`, which PHP 8.6 deprecates

- Support `#[\Override]` on class constants and enum cases (PHP 8.6): `PhanCommentOverrideOnNonOverrideConstant` is emitted when no constant of a parent class or interface is overridden, which is a fatal error in PHP, and `PhanCompatibleOverrideAttribute` when `target_php_version` is older than 8.6. A private constant of a parent class and a constant of a trait used by the class no longer count as overridden, also for `@override`. The constants of a trait are now checked for each class using the trait instead of for the trait itself, as PHP does: they may override a constant of the parent class or of an interface of that class

- Cache the hash of an AST node (`ASTHasher::hash()`) in a `WeakMap` instead of a dynamic property of the node. PHP allocates a property table of 376 bytes for the first dynamic property of an object, and the hash was the only dynamic property of most of the nodes that had one: in Phan's analysis of itself, 27 % of the nodes of an analyzed file had a dynamic property, and 5 % do now. The saving in peak memory is small (2 MB of 724 MB for that run), because few of those nodes are alive at the same time. A modified clone of a hashed node no longer keeps the hash of the original node ([#5638](https://github.com/phan/phan/issues/5638))

+- Fix the inferred type of a chain of three or more pipes (PHP 8.5), such as `$i |> abs(...) |> strval(...) |> strlen(...) |> strval(...)`, which could be the type of an earlier stage (`int` instead of `string` here). Phan caches the types of nodes by object id, and created a new temporary call node for a pipe each time it was looked at, which could get the id and the cached type of an earlier one
+- Use the name of a parameter of a closure type that declares one (`Closure(int $count):void`) in the issues about arguments of calls to it, instead of `$p0`, `$p1`, ...

- Fix a crash of the fallback parser (`--use-fallback-parser`, `--force-polyfill-parser`, the language server) in PHP 8.6 for a binary, octal or hexadecimal integer literal that does not fit in an int, such as `0xffffffffffffffff`: `bindec()`, `hexdec()` and `octdec()` emit a notice for such a number in PHP 8.6. The fallback parser now converts these literals to the same float as php does, which it did not for binary literals (`bindec()` rounds differently) or for hexadecimal literals containing the digit `e`

- Fix false positive `PhanUnreferencedClass` with `--dead-code-detection` and `PHPUnitNotDeadCodePlugin` for every test case class: the reference the plugin added to the class was ignored as a reference from within the class itself ([#5629](https://github.com/phan/phan/issues/5629))

- Fix false positive `PhanWriteOnlyPrivateProperty`, `PhanReadOnlyPrivateProperty`, `PhanUnreferencedPrivateProperty`, `PhanUnreferencedPrivateMethod` and `PhanUnreferencedPrivateClassConstant` with `--dead-code-detection` for a property, method or constant (PHP 8.2+) that a class declares with the same name as a property, an abstract or concrete method, a `@method` or a constant of a trait it uses: `$this->prop`, `$this->method()` and `self::X` in the trait now count as references to the class's declaration, as they already did for a `@property` of the trait. Uses of the class's property or constant also count as references to the trait's declaration of the same name, as they do when the class does not redeclare it, so a trait property that is only written through the class's declaration is no longer reported as `PhanReadOnlyPrivateTraitProperty`. This also applies to traits used through other traits ([#5630](https://github.com/phan/phan/issues/5630))

+ * Utilities for the arguments of a node of kind ast\AST_CALLABLE_CONVERT:
+ * first-class callable syntax (`f(...)`) and php 8.6 partial function application (`f(1, ?)`, `f(1, ...)`, `f(a: ?, b: 2)`).
+ * In AST version 130, the node has a child 'args' of kind ast\AST_ARG_LIST. Its elements are argument expressions,
+ * ast\AST_NAMED_ARG nodes (the expression of which may be a placeholder), and placeholders: nodes of kind ast\AST_PLACEHOLDER_ARG,
+ * with the flag ast\flags\PLACEHOLDER_VARIADIC for `...`. `f(...)` has a single variadic placeholder.
+ * In older AST versions, the node has no children: partial function application cannot be told apart from `f(...)`

+     * @return list<Node|string|int|float> the arguments, including the placeholders

+     * @return bool whether this is the placeholder `...`

+     * @return bool whether this is partial function application: there is an argument other than a single `...`

+     * Null for anything else, including `...` after a named argument.
+                    // `...` after a named argument, e.g. `f(b: 1, ...)`: the remaining parameters are not at this position.
+     * Returns the type of the closure created by partial application of $function.
+     * The parameters of the closure are, in this order:
